glmGamPoi2 performance optimizations

Source: vignettes/perf_optim.Rmd
perf_optim.Rmd

glmGamPoi2 fork

The glmGamPoi2 package is a fork of the existing glmGamPoi package which aims to optimize performance and memory use. Multiple “knobs” are provided which can be used to enable the various implementations provided.

Primarily, the glm_gp entrypoint now has an added perf_optim parameter, which can be used to enable/disable specific optimizations at will.

Currently supported parameters

We demonstrate below the various parameters currently introduced via the perf_optim parameter. First, we load the library, initialize a synthetic dataset, and generate a reference object:

library(glmGamPoi2)

counts <- matrix(rnbinom(256, mu = 4, size = 0.25), 32, 8)
fit_ref <- glm_gp(counts, perf_optim = FALSE)

offset_as_vec

The offset_as_vec parameter allows representing the per-gene/per-observation offsets as a vector when they are not configured to vary across any one observation:

head(fit_ref[["Offset"]]) # we can see this is a matrix
#>            [,1]      [,2]     [,3]       [,4]      [,5]       [,6]        [,7]
#> [1,] -0.1999854 0.3962198 0.161028 -0.3650651 0.1145079 -0.1784792 -0.09680116
#> [2,] -0.1999854 0.3962198 0.161028 -0.3650651 0.1145079 -0.1784792 -0.09680116
#> [3,] -0.1999854 0.3962198 0.161028 -0.3650651 0.1145079 -0.1784792 -0.09680116
#> [4,] -0.1999854 0.3962198 0.161028 -0.3650651 0.1145079 -0.1784792 -0.09680116
#> [5,] -0.1999854 0.3962198 0.161028 -0.3650651 0.1145079 -0.1784792 -0.09680116
#> [6,] -0.1999854 0.3962198 0.161028 -0.3650651 0.1145079 -0.1784792 -0.09680116
#>           [,8]
#> [1,] 0.1685752
#> [2,] 0.1685752
#> [3,] 0.1685752
#> [4,] 0.1685752
#> [5,] 0.1685752
#> [6,] 0.1685752

fit_vec <- glm_gp(counts, perf_optim = list(offset_as_vec = TRUE))
head(fit_vec[["Offset"]]) # we can see this is now a vector
#> [1] -0.1999854  0.3962198  0.1610280 -0.3650651  0.1145079 -0.1784792

delay_mu

The delay_mu parameter allows representing the prediction matrix Mu via a thunk interface instead of eagerly computing a dense representation:

head(fit_ref[["Mu"]]) # we can see this is a matrix
#>          [,1]     [,2]     [,3]     [,4]     [,5]     [,6]     [,7]     [,8]
#> [1,] 1.556401 2.825206 2.233097 1.319557 2.131593 1.590236 1.725575 2.250015
#> [2,] 3.140700 5.701054 4.506222 2.662768 4.301394 3.208977 3.482081 4.540360
#> [3,] 2.719190 4.935922 3.901447 2.305401 3.724109 2.778303 3.014755 3.931003
#> [4,] 3.871690 7.027959 5.555034 3.282520 5.302532 3.955857 4.292526 5.597117
#> [5,] 4.504430 8.176520 6.462878 3.818973 6.169111 4.602352 4.994042 6.511839
#> [6,] 3.097058 5.621833 4.443605 2.625767 4.241623 3.164385 3.433695 4.477269

fit_delayed <- glm_gp(counts, perf_optim = list(delay_mu = TRUE))

is.function(fit_delayed[["Mu"]]) # we can see this is now a _function_
#> [1] TRUE

# demonstration of the thunk'd Mu API
all.equal(fit_delayed[["Mu"]](), fit_ref[["Mu"]])
#> [1] TRUE
all.equal(fit_delayed[["Mu"]](i = 1L), fit_ref[["Mu"]][1, , drop = FALSE])
#> [1] TRUE
all.equal(fit_delayed[["Mu"]](j = 1L), fit_ref[["Mu"]][, 1, drop = FALSE])
#> [1] TRUE
all.equal(fit_delayed[["Mu"]](1L, 1L), fit_ref[["Mu"]][1, 1, drop = FALSE])
#> [1] TRUE

use_nr_overdisp_impl and do_parallel

The use_nr_overdisp_impl and do_parallel flags do not change output shape, but modify behaviour of internal routines:

  • use_nr_overdisp_impl: enables the use of an alternative overdispersion estimation routine written in C++
  • do_parallel: enables parallelization of various steps across the package

Please note that while testing/benchmarking has found that these do not significantly affect result outputs, there are edge cases (especially for ill-conditioned fits with high deviance on the resulting fit) where enabling use_nr_overdisp_impl can lead to slightly different results.

fit_alt <- glm_gp(counts, perf_optim = list(do_parallel = 2L, use_nr_overdisp_impl = TRUE))

# we can see these have no effect on resulting model parameters
all.equal(fit_alt[["overdispersions"]], fit_ref[["overdispersions"]])
#> [1] TRUE
all.equal(fit_alt[["Beta"]], fit_ref[["Beta"]])
#> [1] TRUE

Changing package-wide defaults

Finally, to improve usability when one wishes to change parameters package wide, the set_perf_optim_opts helper is provided. Notably, it has a v2 parameter, which allows for a coarse-grain toggle of all recommended optimizations:

set_perf_optim_opts(v2 = TRUE)

get_perf_optim_opts()
#> $offset_as_vec
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $do_parallel
#> [1] 4
#> 
#> $delay_mu
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $use_nr_overdisp_impl
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $cast_dgC_Y_to_dgR
#> [1] FALSE

fit_v2 <- glm_gp(counts)

# we can see that all optimizations have now been enabled
head(fit_v2[["Offset"]])
#> [1] -0.1999854  0.3962198  0.1610280 -0.3650651  0.1145079 -0.1784792
is.function(fit_v2[["Mu"]])
#> [1] TRUE
